input.question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?
input.ground_truth: Not so much a boosted immune system, but polio affected the upper and middle class far worse than the lower class because kids were exposed to the virus early on in low income areas. As a consequence they became immune to it, while the upper class kids were exposed later in life when it had a far more deleterious effect. [source](_URL_0_)

Question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?

Okay! Imagine your body has little soldiers called "immune cells" that help you stay healthy and fight germs. Some people think that if you eat a little bit of dirt when you're a kid, your immune soldiers get to practice and become stronger, so you don't get sick as often.

But here's what scientists have found: There’s no special proof that eating dirt makes your immune system better. In fact, eating dirt can be dangerous because there might be bad germs or yucky things in the dirt that can make you sick.

So, even though playing outside and getting a little bit of dirt on your hands is okay, you should NOT eat dirt. Your immune system learns and gets strong in other ways, like when you get a little sick sometimes or when you wash your hands and stay clean.

So, eating dirt is not a good idea, even if you want your immune soldiers to be strong!
